note: Olli asked what the card stroke outline was and said that while he likes having an outline, the current one feels a bit harsh on the cards against the white background. Investigation confirmed his instinct was more than aesthetic: the outline used a homepage-local bespoke value, rgba(25, 25, 25, .42) -- a ~42 percent charcoal rendering as a hard mid-grey line against F8 -- that appears nowhere else in the repository. The canonical Product Card 02 that the hero cards descend from contains its material with a soft shadow and only 12 percent-opacity internal lines, never a hard outer stroke, and the foundation's own border tokens are far softer (--mz-border-default #DADAD6, --mz-border-strong #8A8A84). So the gradient cards were wearing a heavier, non-canonical edge than every other card in the system, including the white cards on the same page.

sections.title: Hero
sections.feedback: Keep an outline on the cards but soften it -- the current dark stroke feels harsh on white. Bind it to the canonical border token rather than a bespoke charcoal value.

consistencyFinding.priorValueScope: homepage-local; appears in no other repository file
consistencyFinding.canonicalReference: The QC04 landing card uses a soft containment shadow plus 12%-opacity internal lines, not a hard outer stroke; the foundation border tokens are --mz-border-default #DADAD6 and --mz-border-strong #8A8A84.
consistencyFinding.resolution: The --card-outline variable now binds to the canonical foundation token var(--mz-border-default) (#DADAD6) rather than a bespoke literal. This softens the edge and, more importantly, makes the gradient cards use the same border every other card on the page already uses (--page-line is the same value). A visible hairline is retained deliberately -- the hero cards overlap in the fan and the ethos bans ambient card shadows, so a line is the correct containment device; it was only too heavy.
